manifests.title: Numerator-denominator role map
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Domain of x/(x^2-x-6). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: x≠3,-2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: Domain intervals
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Factor the denominator, solve Q=0, record exclusions, and partition the domain into intervals of continuity. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: No-real-zero denominator
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is simplifying before recording the original exclusions. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify rational functions and determine all excluded inputs from the original denominator before simplifying.

manifests.title: Cancellation with domain memory
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze (x^2-9)/(x-3). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Line y=x+3 with hole (3,6).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: Hole coordinate construction
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Factor, retain original exclusions, cancel, and evaluate the simplified formula at the cancelled input to locate the hole. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: Equal expressions versus functions
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is filling the hole because the simplified formula has a value there. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Identify removable discontinuities caused by common factors and distinguish formula equivalence from function equality.

manifests.title: One-sided arrows
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze 1/(x-2) near 2. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Left -∞, right +∞.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Multiplicity comparison
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Simplify common factors, identify remaining denominator zeros, and use local factor signs and multiplicity to state each side. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Local sign ledger
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is treating an asymptote as a function point or assuming both sides behave alike. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine vertical asymptotes and describe one-sided behavior from factor signs and multiplicity.

manifests.title: Degree comparison chart
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze (5x^3-2)/(2x^3+x). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Horizontal asymptote y=5/2.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Leading-term quotient
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Use y=0 when numerator degree is lower, leading coefficient ratio when degrees match, and division when numerator degree is higher. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Asymptote crossing
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is applying the equal-degree ratio to unequal degrees. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Determine horizontal asymptotes from degree comparison and interpret them as long-run output behavior.

manifests.title: Division decomposition
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze (x^2+1)/(x-1). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: x+1+2/(x-1), so asymptote y=x+1.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.title: Slant approach
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Write R=Q+remainder/divisor; the graph approaches y=Q as the proper remainder term approaches zero. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.title: Polynomial asymptote
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is claiming the rational function equals the quotient everywhere. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Use polynomial division to determine nonhorizontal asymptotes and describe the shrinking remainder term.

manifests.title: Rational sign chart
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze signs of (x-1)/(x+2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Positive, negative, positive across -2 and 1.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.title: Intercept versus hole
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Factor, classify zeros as intercepts, holes, or asymptotes, test one input per interval, and calculate the y-intercept if allowed. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.title: Multiplicity at rational zero
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is counting a cancelled numerator zero as an intercept. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Find rational intercepts and determine positive and negative intervals using factored sign structure.

manifests.title: Complete checklist
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Analyze (x+1)/(x-2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: VA x=2, HA y=1, x-intercept -1, y-intercept -1/2, signs +,-,+.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

manifests.title: Branch assembly
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Build a feature ledger, sketch each continuity interval separately, state one-sided behavior, and verify with technology. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

manifests.title: Window failure comparison
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is omitting a hole or connecting branches across a vertical asymptote. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Construct a complete rational graph using domain, discontinuities, asymptotes, intercepts, signs, and selected values.

manifests.title: Intersection equation
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve (x+1)/(x-2)=3/(x-2). Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: Candidate x=2 is excluded, so no solution.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

manifests.title: Candidate filter
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Record restrictions, multiply every term by an LCD, solve the resulting equation, and reject excluded candidates. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

manifests.title: Exact-numerical method tree
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is accepting every solution of the cleared equation. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational equations and intersections exactly or numerically while rejecting excluded candidates.

manifests.title: Inequality sign chart
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Solve (x+3)/(x-4)≤0. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: [-3,4).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

manifests.title: Endpoint rules
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Move all terms to one side, combine and factor, list numerator and denominator zeros, test intervals, and apply endpoint rules. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

manifests.title: Function comparison
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is multiplying by a denominator whose sign changes across the domain. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Solve rational inequalities using critical values, sign intervals, and correct endpoint inclusion.

manifests.title: Variation relationship map
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: y varies inversely with x; y=5 at x=8. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: y=40/x.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

manifests.title: Positive-domain inverse model
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Translate the wording into a formula with constant k, use a known data point to find k, and interpret how output responds to input changes. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

manifests.title: Units of k
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is placing a factor in the numerator or denominator contrary to the wording. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Build and interpret direct, inverse, joint, and combined variation models with meaningful parameters and domains.

manifests.title: Denominator-component map
manifests.description: Depict the foundation problem exactly: Decompose 1/[x(x+1)]. Show the quantities, axes, intervals, or algebraic objects needed to reach this conclusion: 1/x-1/(x+1).
manifests.learnerOutcome: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

manifests.title: Strategic substitution
manifests.description: Visualize the mechanism explicitly: Divide first if needed, factor the denominator, write every required component, clear denominators, solve coefficients, and recombine to verify. The figure must show intermediate states or mappings, not merely the final formula.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.

manifests.title: Recombination check
manifests.description: Place the correct structure beside the invalid move described here: A frequent error is omitting a repeated-power term. Mark the first point where the conclusions diverge.
manifests.learnerOutcome: Decompose proper rational functions with factorable denominators into simpler component fractions and verify recombination.
